concerns.text: FR-003 states the residual‑stress proxy is used ONLY for Feature Set C construction (process + material), while FR-004 defines Feature Set C as “process + material properties” (i.e., without residual stress). Later FR-012 also treats the proxy as part of Feature Set C for predictive comparison. This creates a contradictory definition of what Feature Set C contains.

FR-001 specifies the unified schema includes columns for material type, process parameters, residual stress, and fatigue life cycles, but omits material‑property columns (e.g., yield strength, hardness) required for Feature Set C as described in the idea and FR‑004.

FR-003 states the residual‑stress proxy is used ONLY for Feature Set C construction, whereas the original idea allows the proxy to be used in stress‑mediated models (Feature Set B) when measured stress is missing. This redefines the analysis plan and limits the ability to assess predictive value of stress‑mediated features, constituting a drift from the research question.

The plan imposes a hard ≥ 50 measured‑stress rows threshold for mediation analysis but provides no a priori power analysis or effect‑size justification; without a formal power calculation the sample may be insufficient to detect a meaningful indirect effect, risking inconclusive or biased mediation results.

The residual‑stress proxy (σ_res ≈ k·heat_input·cooling_rate) is used in Feature Set C and in predictive performance comparisons, yet the specification does not address its construct validity or potential bias; mixing proxy‑derived stress with measured stress can confound attribution of any performance gain to “stress‑mediated” features.

FR‑008 calls for paired t‑tests on absolute error differences between models A and B. The normality assumption for the difference distribution is not justified; with potentially skewed error distributions a non‑parametric alternative (e.g., Wilcoxon signed‑rank) or bootstrapped confidence intervals would be more robust.

responses.response: Clarified Feature Set C to include material properties *and* the estimated residual stress proxy; updated FR-003, FR-004, and FR-012 to use the same definition and removed contradictory wording.
responses.what_changed: FR-003 wording, FR-004 definition, FR-012 reference; added explanation of proxy use.

responses.response: Extended the unified schema in FR-001 to include material‑property columns (e.g., yield strength, hardness) required for Feature Set C.
Allowed the residual‑stress proxy to be used in Feature Set B when measured stress is missing, matching the original idea, and documented this in FR-003.
responses.what_changed: FR-003 now states proxy may augment Feature Set B and is required for Feature Set C.

responses.response: Added an a‑priori power analysis justification for the ≥ 50 measured‑stress rows threshold and introduced FR-013 to require reporting the analysis.
responses.what_changed: Edge case description expanded, new FR-013 added.

responses.response: Added FR-014 to evaluate construct validity of the proxy (correlation with measured stress) and referenced it in FR-003.
responses.what_changed: New FR-014 added, FR-003 mentions validation step.

responses.response: Replaced paired t‑test with Wilcoxon signed‑rank test (non‑parametric) and updated FR-008 accordingly.
responses.what_changed: FR-008 wording changed to specify Wilcoxon test or bootstrapped CI.
